cost-per-success.name: Cost per 1,000 Successes
cost-per-success.meaning: The successful trials’ cost is divided by their count, then scaled to the stated comparison unit.

example.template: A ${param:concept.example.values.cost} cost for {param:concept.example.values.successes} successes gives ${param:concept.example.values.result} per {param:concept.example.values.scale} successes.

trial-counts.name: Trial Counts
trial-counts.meaning: Each benchmark runs until it has its intended number of successful trials, unless a serious blocker stops it.

price-sheet.name: Price Sheet
price-sheet.meaning: The price sheet records public list rates and the billing conditions that qualify them.

example.template: A listed ${param:concept.example.values.rate} hourly rate gives a ${param:concept.example.values.result} charge for {param:concept.example.values.hours} hours.

elapsed-time.name: Elapsed Time
elapsed-time.meaning: Elapsed time records the duration between the benchmark’s declared start and stop events.

example.template: A request sent at {param:concept.example.values.start} s and returned at {param:concept.example.values.stop} s took {param:concept.example.values.elapsed} s.

ranking-floor.name: Ranking Floor
ranking-floor.meaning: A benchmark can require a minimum number of successful trials before a result enters its ranking.

example.template: With a floor of {param:concept.example.values.floor}, {param:concept.example.values.successes} successes need {param:concept.example.values.more} more successful trial.
